title: UN Chief Warns of 'Virus of Indifference' as Ebola Funding Gap Widens to $1.1B
detail: UN Secretary-General António Guterres told the Security Council on 27 August 2026 that the world must overcome 'the virus of indifference' in responding to DRC's Ebola outbreak — now the largest in the country's history, with more than 5,600 cases and 2,700 deaths since the mid-May declaration and roughly 500 new cases reported every week. Guterres said the humanitarian response is only 48% funded and appealed for an additional $1.1 billion, warning that 'without additional funding, vital operations will run out of money' within weeks. He said fighting and displacement in Ituri Province have uprooted roughly 1 million people, more than 40 healthcare workers have been killed, and treatment centers and ambulances have come under attack, even as community engagement — including artists, influencers, religious leaders and former combatants — has expanded awareness efforts. He also noted that WHO had just declared Uganda's linked outbreak over.

media.caption: UN Secretary-General António Guterres warns the world must overcome 'the virus of indifference' as DRC's Ebola outbreak funding gap widens

title: DRC Launches Ebola Vaccination Campaign for Frontline Workers Under Compassionate-Use Framework
detail: DRC Health Minister Roger Kamba launched an Ervebo (rVSV-ZEBOV) vaccination campaign on Thursday, 27 August 2026 in Kisangani, capital of Tshopo province, to protect frontline responders against the country's worst-ever Ebola outbreak. 'We have decided to use the Ervebo vaccine to protect first those who are on the front line, therefore our health care providers, but also people who have been in contact with patients,' Kamba said. The rollout covers 14 health zones across Tshopo, Bas-Uélé and Haut-Uélé provinces, drawing on the 50,000 doses (of 70,000 allocated by the ICG on 20 August) set aside for frontline and health workers, distinct from the separate 20,000-dose Phase 3 clinical trial testing cross-protection against Bundibugyo virus. The vaccine is being administered under a compassionate-use framework rather than as a fully licensed indication, since Ervebo is approved against Zaire ebolavirus, not the Bundibugyo strain driving this outbreak.

media.caption: Congo begins Ebola vaccinations for frontline health workers in Kisangani
